newsitem.title: UK: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Oct 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Financial Times - Oct 8.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
-- BANKS TO TAKE 45.5 PERCENT STAKE IN EUROTUNNEL

Details revealed on Monday of a restructuring deal for Eurotunnel include plans for lender banks to take a 45.5 percent stake in the company which currently has debts of 9.1 billion stg. The deal ends a lengthy period of discussions on debt reduction and staves off the prospect of the company being placed into administration. The deal was described by Eurotunnel chairman Sir Alastair Morton as an "acceptable compromise".
-- MAJOR TARGETS BENEFIT FRAUD

A central theme for this year's Conservative party conference in Bournemouth will be government plans for reform of the social welfare system which will include measures designed to reduce levels of fraud. Measures being considered include the restriction of rights to future benefits for those found guilty of fraud. Speaking on the eve of the conference, Prime Minister John Major stressed that in order to create a system which provided "opportunity for all", it was essential to create an affordable benefits system.
-- TIETMEYER WARNS ON SHORT-TERM EFFORTS TO JOIN EMU

The president of the German Bundesbank, Hans Tietmeyer, has expressed his concern about some EU member states adopting severe budget strategies in order to qualify for participation in the planned single currency. He noted that there was a danger that economic benefits derived from such measures might prove short-term. Tietmeyer also once more spoke of German opposition to non-single currency member states being provided with equal access to the target currency payments system.
-- SHELL AND TEXACO PLAN US ALLIANCE

Shell and Texaco have announced plans to combine some of their US oil refining and marketing activities. The companies hope to reap as much as 2 billion dollars a year through savings and efficiencies brought about by the deal, which follows a similar decision in the European market by BP and Mobil. Talks on the finer details of the Shell/Texaco arrangement are expected to prove complex and may take several months to conclude.
-- DAF TRUCKS TAKEN OVER BY PACCAR IN 348.5 MILLION STG DEAL

The third-largest US truck manufacturer, Paccar, has acquired Daf Trucks, a Dutch-Belgian group, in an agreed deal worth some 348.5 million stg. It is thought that the deal is likely to receive the necessary approval from the European governments concerned. The deal, according to Daf chairman Cor Baan will provide the company with additional financial and technological resources and is seen as another example of a process of rationalisation taking place in the European trucks sector.
-- BRITISH GAS MAY FACE WIDER PROBE BY MMC

The UK's gas industry regulator Ofgas has announced that it may ask the Monopolies & Mergers Commission to examine whether or not plans by British Gas to combine its international exploration and production unit with Transco, the division that operates its pipeline infrastructure, runs contrary to public interest. The company might, as a result, be asked either to divest the exploration unit or to ring-fence it from Transco. The MMC is currently assessing price controls proposed by Ofgas but last week rejected by British Gas.
-- SETBACK FOR MANUFACTURING INDUSTRY AS PRODUCTION FALLS

Figures from the Office for National Statistics reveal that during August UK manufacturing output fell at its fastest rate for over three years. While the figures will prove a setback for government hopes of a widespread economic recovery, they will also provide support for Chancellor Kenneth Clarke's resistance to Bank of England pressure for a rise in interest rates. The latest manufacturing figures were dismissed by the Treasury as an erratic monthly movement.
-- BOTNAR IN 59 MILLION STG TAX SETTLEMENT WITH INLAND REVENUE

Octav Botnar, the founder of Nissan UK, who on Monday reached an agreement to pay the UK tax authorities some 59 million stg to settle a five-year tax dispute, is still reported to be facing the prospect of arrest should he return from exile in Switzerland. While the tax claim has been dropped by the Inland Revenue, Botnar still faces allegations of fraud. Botnar's company at one point had sole rights to import Nissan motor vehicles into the UK, though this arrangement ended in 1990 when Nissan established its own distribution network.
-- BRITISH COMPANY PRACTICE PRAISED

A corporate governance survey carried out by Belgian consultancy Deminor has concluded that UK companies accord their shareholders better treatment than other EU rivals. British companies were rated highly in the area of disclosure of executive pay. The survey ranked Dutch companies last, though noted that legislative changes planned in France would allow its corporate sector to challenge the UK for top position.
-- SCOTLAND WINS 1 BILLION STG KOREAN FACTORY

The South Korean electronics company Hyundai has announced that it is to invest one billion stg in setting up a new semiconductor manufacturing facility at Dumferline, Scotland. The venture is expected to result in the creation of at least 700 jobs and will begin operations from 1999. The news comes months after LG Electronics, also of Korea, announced that it was to locate a 2.6 billion dollar chip and consumer electronics plant in south Wales.
